prompt: Training 65-year-olds to use computers would be a good use of government money. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
essay:
It is often argued that using government money to train people aged 65 and above to use computers would be a worthwhile investment. I strongly agree with this view because digital skills can help older people access essential services independently and maintain communication with family and friends.

On the one hand, computer training can help older people remain independent in a society where many essential services are becoming digital. Banks, government departments and healthcare providers increasingly offer online services, so basic computer skills can make everyday tasks easier for elderly citizens. For example, a 65-year-old person who understands online banking can check an account or pay a bill without travelling to a bank branch. Similarly, basic digital knowledge can help older people book medical appointments and access government information. As a result, training can provide them with greater independence and reduce their reliance on family members.

Another important benefit is improved communication and social connection. Older people who learn to use computers can communicate with relatives and friends through email, video calls and social media. This is particularly useful when family members live in different cities or countries. For instance, an elderly parent can make regular video calls with children who live abroad, allowing them to maintain a close relationship despite the physical distance. In this way, digital skills can reduce social isolation and improve emotional well-being. Although some older people may need additional support when learning new technology, the long-term social and practical benefits justify public investment.

In conclusion, I strongly agree that using government money to train people aged 65 and above to use computers would be worthwhile. Such training can increase their independence in accessing essential services and help them maintain meaningful relationships with family and friends.
